sentences.text: Shri S.N. Saraf, counsel for the petitioner.

Shri D.K. Paroha, Panel Lawyer for the
respondent/State.
Heard on I.A.No.3112/2017 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the petitioner Peetu Yadav.

A perusal of the record reveals that petitioner has been convicted under Section 7 (2) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 6 months and a fine in the sum of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation.

It has been submitted on behalf of the petitioner that petitioner was on bail during trial and he has been in jail since 07.02.2017; therefore, it has been prayed that the application be allowed and petitioner be released on bail.
Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State has opposed the application.
However, keeping in view the quantum of sentence imposed upon the petitioner and the period already undergone by him, he deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Consequently, this application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of petitioner Peetu Yadav is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount and furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.40,000/- with one solvent surety in the same amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 18.09.2017 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard, the substantive jail sentence imposed upon the petitioner shall stand suspended and he shall be released on bail.
A perusal of the memo of revision reveals that the Food and Drugs Administration through the Food Inspector Chhatarpur, has not been made party as a respondent.
Learned counsel for the petitioner prays for time to do needful.
Let appropriate application be moved for rectifying aforesaid default within a week.
